regions.label: East Africa

Kenya's new USD 38bn National Infrastructure Fund is the one to watch for a shift toward domestically financed procurement.

leads.evidence_window: L&T Energy Hydrocarbon Onshore signs ultra-mega gas compression EPC contract in the Middle East. L&T Energy Hydrocarbon Onshore has signed the contract for a gas compression facilities project for a client in the Middle East against a letter of award issued in FY26. The project involves engineering, procurement and construction of gas compression plants comprising gas inlet facilities, gas compression systems, condensate and produced water handling systems, propane refrigeration systems and associated utilities. The facilities will be developed for new onshore installations to process sour gas. To meet power requirements, the L&T Power Transmission and Distribution business will execute two 230 kV extra-high-voltage substations. The contract marks the start of a strategically important project that will add significant gas compression capacity and utility infrastructure, said E S Sathyanarayanan, Senior Vice President and Head of L&T Energy Hydrocarbon Onshore. Larsen & Toubro is a USD 32 billion Indian multinational engaged in EPC projects, hi-tech manufacturing, products and services.

regions.label: South East Asia
macro_lines: Vietnam is targeting a late-2026 groundbreaking on the 1,541 km, USD 67bn North-South high-speed railway having already delivered 3,513 km of expressway. Indonesia's Trans-Sumatra programme and a 2,461 km toll-road target to 2029 keep the concession pipeline rolling. The binding constraint across the region is contractor and plant-fleet capacity, not demand — six countries are competing for the same machinery and crews, which is a supply opening rather than a risk.

regions.label: Latin America
macro_lines: Mining investment across the region ran above USD 18bn in 2023 and logistics is taking a rising share of it, as operators accept that extraction without export capacity strands the asset. Chilean and Peruvian highway widening in the northern mining districts is being sized for heavy-vehicle freight, and access-road build-out remains the first capital call on any new deposit.

leads.project_name: SANY Group ships first autonomous mining truck fleet to South America
leads.source_title: SANY Group ships first autonomous mining truck fleet to South America
leads.evidence_window: SANY Group ships first autonomous mining truck fleet to South America. SANY Group has shipped its first batch of SKT110Ei pure-electric autonomous mining trucks to South America, its first autonomous mining project in Latin America. The scope covers an autonomous truck fleet, an intelligent dispatching system and lifecycle operations and maintenance services tailored to local operating conditions. The solution integrates autonomous trucks, roadside infrastructure and cloud dispatching, aimed at haulage safety, operator shortages and rising labour costs. SANY Intelligent Mining, a subsidiary of SANY International, had deployed more than 300 autonomous mining trucks globally as of July 2026. Separately, Codelco has announced multi-billion-dollar upgrades to its smelting and refining facilities in Chile to support a transition to electric mining fleets, and plans to fully electrify its underground fleet. Total mining investment across Latin America exceeded USD 18 billion in 2023, with logistics infrastructure capturing a growing share as operators recognise that extraction capacity without export capacity strands operational leverage.

Buying runs through EBRD, EIB and World Bank procurement rules, so local-content and after-sales servicing commitments decide awards as much as unit price.

macro_lines: FDI inflows ran at 6.3% of GDP in 2024 — 4.2% excluding Guyana, where oil has pushed inflows to around 35% of GDP. Preliminary 2025 figures put Suriname near 30% on the back of the GranMorgu offshore development. Fiscal space is thin outside those two, so most of the build pipeline is DFI-financed and moves at procurement speed rather than corporate speed.

regions.label: Western Europe
macro_lines: EU truck registrations rose 9.8% in H1 2026 to 171,933 units and vans 1.9% to 742,759, recovering from a weak 2025 base. Diesel still took 92.1% of truck volume. Buses were the standout at +22.7%, with electric bus share up from 21.6% to 27.7%. Growth was concentrated in Central and Eastern European demand, not the big four Western markets, where Germany, Italy and France all fell on vans.
